story: Gary is heading out onto Magnolia Loop with a determined stride, while Donna sits at home cheerfully checking her phone to see whether he has texted back about Tuesday's court time. Out on the street, Hal is focused on counting the pink flamingos in the yard flock and comparing the tally against the three-flamingo limit for lot L-02. Back in her kitchen, Rosa is hopeful as she goes through the pantry and fridge, labeling her sofrito and marinade and jotting down a shopping list for Friday's dinner.
events: Gary headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Donna (donna phone): Check whether Gary texted back to confirm Tuesday's court time
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count each flamingo visible from the street and write down an exact tally against L-02's limit of three
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Check the pantry and fridge, label the sofrito and marinade, and jot a shopping list for Friday's dinner

gary.thought_process: I filled out the review form last tick with my measurements and sketch. That form is basically done, and under L-01 the lights and speaker mounts visible from the street need Architectural Review approval before I bolt anything down for the parade. Hal offered to check it line by line, but nobody's around and I've been puttering at the workbench all morning. The form has to get to the review, and moving to Magnolia Loop is the way to find Hal or whoever handles it. Better to get it in now than sit stewing, and on the way I might run into someone to chat with. I'll hold off on permanent mounting and keep the sound system off the amps until quiet hours aren't an issue.

parameters.content: Heading out to find Hal and get my cart review form checked and submitted for Architectural Review

donna.thought_process: Court slot is already penciled in and the spare paddle is packed. Gary isn't here, and I just texted him the time. I shouldn't keep fussing with the same calendar and bag. Gary's still brand new, so a little extra prep would help him: I could tuck a beginner's tip sheet and a ball into the bag, or just use my phone to check whether he's confirmed Tuesday. Last tick I confirmed the calendar, so the phone is the natural next step to see if Gary texted back and then get on with my day.

parameters.content: Check whether Gary texted back to confirm Tuesday's court time

hal.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop with binoculars in hand and nobody in sight. I've already queued up two flamingo counts in my recent memories but haven't written a clean tally yet. A proper count against L-02 is the honest groundwork before I go reporting anyone, and I promised myself to stay fair with Donna. No guessing, no padding the number. Count first, then decide whether it goes to the committee.

parameters.content: Count each flamingo visible from the street and write down an exact tally against L-02's limit of three

rosa.thought_process: I've already prepped the sofrito, marinade, and table, and checked my shifts against Thursday coffee and Friday's dinner. No neighbors are in sight, so there's nobody to talk to. The next useful step is the kitchen: portion and label what I've prepped, then work out what still needs to be bought or made ahead so Friday isn't a scramble. I want this welcome dinner to land, with all three neighbors at one table.

parameters.content: Check the pantry and fridge, label the sofrito and marinade, and jot a shopping list for Friday's dinner

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
